stem: The hybridisation of the central sulphur atom in sulphurous acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$, is:

verdicts.working: H₂SO₃ has three S–O σ bonds and one lone pair on sulfur: four electron domains, corresponding to sp³ hybridisation.

working:
$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ has three $\text{S–O}$ sigma bonds and one lone pair on S.
Steric number $=3+1=4$; hybridisation $=sp^3$.

Independent check: H₂SO₃ has three S–O σ bonds and one lone pair on sulfur: four electron domains, corresponding to sp³ hybridisation.
solution:
Sulphur in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ has three $\text{S–O}$ $\sigma$ bonds and one lone pair.
$$\text{Steric number}=3+1=4\;\Rightarrow\;\text{hybridisation}=sp^3$$
